title: JVM Memory Areas: Heap, Stack, Metaspace

scenes.line1: Where does your Java data live?
scenes.say: Ever wonder where your Java data actually lives? Is it on the heap, the stack, or in metaspace?

scenes.label: Heap
scenes.sub: Stores objects. Managed by garbage collection.
scenes.say: The heap is where Java stores objects. It's managed by garbage collection, so you don't free memory yourself.
The stack holds method calls and local variables for each thread. The heap is shared, storing objects for the whole app.

scenes.label: Metaspace
scenes.say: Metaspace is where the Java Virtual Machine keeps class definitions and metadata. It grows as needed.

scenes.question: Where are local variables stored?
scenes.right: On the stack, which is thread-local.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: local variables aren't on the heap. They're on the stack, and each thread has its own stack.
